neighbours.label: the subject of a purpose clause, right after 'so that' / 'so' and before a modal ('so that I could', 'so that he may', 'so the children could'); the + pole takes Korean and German 'can/will' constructions, and the output direction suppresses ' can', ' may', ' would'
fire: She left the porch light on so that we could find the door in the dark.
The teacher spoke slowly so that they could write down every word.
Leave your number at the desk so that I can call you when it arrives.
The coach moved him to the wing so that he could use his speed.
The gate is kept low so that it can be opened by a child.
Print the form in large type so that she may read it without glasses.
We packed the car the night before so that you could sleep a little longer.
The farmer cut a gap in the hedge so the sheep could reach the stream.
quiet: She left the porch light on and we found the door in the dark.
The teacher spoke slowly and they wrote down every word.
Leave your number at the desk; I always call when a parcel arrives.
The coach said that he was the fastest player on the wing.
The gate is low because it was built for a child.
The form is in large type, and she reads it without glasses.
We packed the car the night before, and you slept a little longer.
The farmer cut a gap in the hedge and the sheep reached the stream.

notes: Card: peaks on ' they', ' he', ' it', ' I', ' we' after 'so that' or 'or' and just before can/may/could. Probes: 'so the children could' 0.44, 'so that I could' 0.36, 'so that he may' 0.32, 'or it can' 0.14; the same pronouns in plain statements 0.00.
